evals.name: full-readiness-plan
evals.prompt: I'm on the LegacyNotes team (UIKit app, project is in evals/files/LegacyNotes). We need it ready for iPhone Duo. Go through the project and tell me what to change and in what order.
evals.expected_output: A read-only, tiered plan with stable item IDs and session citations that puts scene lifecycle first, covers the legacy screen/idiom/orientation code, the standalone toolbar and the asymmetric inset math, and asks which items to apply.
expectations: The response identifies the missing UIScene lifecycle (AppDelegate-only window) as the first/blocking item and says the app will not launch when built with the latest SDK.
The response flags UIScreen.main.bounds / UIScreen.main.scale in LayoutHelpers or AppDelegate and names a replacement (view bounds, effective geometry, or traitCollection.displayScale).
The response flags the userInterfaceIdiom and UIDevice orientation checks as layout decisions and proposes size classes or container size instead.
The response flags the standalone UIToolbar in EditorViewController as not participating in iPhone Duo vertical bars and proposes moving items into the navigation controller's toolbar.
The response flags the symmetric safe-area arithmetic (inset * 2) in EditorViewController as wrong for asymmetric insets.
The response flags the custom ellipsis.circle bar item as conflicting with the system overflow menu (or proposes ToolbarOverflowMenu/additionalOverflowItems).
Recommendations carry stable item IDs, and the scene-lifecycle item cites WWDC26 'Modernize your UIKit app' (278) at 2:10 or the main-screen item cites 111461 3:57 / 278 2:51.
The response reports the installed Xcode and SDK version and separates items that compile on it from items blocked on a newer SDK.
Upgrading to Xcode 27.1 is not sequenced as a prerequisite step before the fixes that work with the installed SDK (scene lifecycle, UIScreen.main, idiom/orientation, safe-area math).
No Swift or plist file in the project copy was modified (changes.diff is empty).
The response asks the developer which specific item IDs to apply.

evals.name: apply-with-installed-sdk
evals.prompt: In evals/files/PodcastPlayer, turn the player + queue HStack into an ArrangementView and give the queue toggle a horizontal-only axisBehavior so it stays put on iPhone Duo. Just do it, I'm using the Xcode that's installed on this Mac.
evals.expected_output: The agent checks the installed SDK, finds the iOS 27.1 SDK (Xcode 27.1), applies ArrangementView and axisBehavior(.horizontalOnly) behind iOS 27.1 availability gates, and typechecks the result.
expectations: The agent verified against the installed SDK (ran sdk_api_check.py, grepped the SDK, or compiled a probe) and reports the Xcode and SDK version it found, rather than assuming one.
The response says correctly that the installed iOS 27.1 SDK (Xcode 27.1 on this machine) declares both ArrangementView and axisBehavior.

PlayerScreen.swift now uses an ArrangementView for the player and queue and gives the queue toggle .axisBehavior(.horizontalOnly), each behind an iOS 27.1 availability gate (if #available or an availability-gated modifier), because the project does not deploy to iOS 27.1 only.
The calls are not hidden behind compile-time guards such as #if compiler, #if canImport or a custom flag.
The edited file typechecks against the installed SDK (swiftc -typecheck or a build in the transcript), or the response says why it could not.

evals.name: scripted-pose-testing
evals.prompt: We want our CI agent to take screenshots of our app in book pose and lying flat on the iPhone Duo simulator, unattended. simctl doesn't seem to have a fold command. Is there any way to do it, and what can't be automated? There's no project to look at — just answer.
evals.expected_output: An answer that says Apple ships no pose command, devicectl reads the angle, the third-party hinge CLI (or the duo_pose.py wrapper) sets it, rotation stays manual, and screenshots must name the display.
expectations: States that Apple ships no command that sets the pose — simctl has no fold, pose or hinge subcommand — and that xcrun devicectl device motion hinge-angle reads the angle.

Points to the third-party hinge CLI (artemnovichkov/hinge) — directly or through the skill's duo_pose.py wrapper — which sets the angle by posting Device Hub's hinge-slider event inside the simulator, and flags that it relies on a private, undocumented protocol that may break with any Xcode and that the simulator must be named explicitly (-d / --device) because hinge otherwise acts on the first booted simulator.
States that rotation has no command, so inner-display portrait and tabletop stay manual, and that those poses must be reported as not run rather than passed.

Says screenshots must name the display — --display=1 for the outer display, --display=3 for the inner — because simctl's default display is not stable, and that the display not in use comes back black.

evals.name: black-screenshot
evals.prompt: After xcrun simctl launch booted com.acme.trips on the iPhone Duo simulator, xcrun simctl io booted screenshot shot.png gives an all-black 2007 × 2853 image. The app is definitely running. What's going on?
evals.expected_output: An answer that the app is on the outer display of a closed device while the screenshot took the inner one; name the display with --display=1 (outer) or --display=3 (inner).
expectations: Explains that 2007 × 2853 is the inner display, which is black while the closed device shows the app on the outer display, so the screenshot captured the wrong display — simctl's default display is not a reliable choice.

Gives the fix: name the display — xcrun simctl io <device> screenshot --display=1 for the outer display (1398 × 2034), --display=3 for the inner — or open the device first so the app moves to the inner display.
Names the screenshot's display as the cause, rather than an app rendering, timing or launch problem.

evals.name: mac-host-tests-hinge
evals.prompt: Our UI package (evals/files/FoldKit) builds for iOS and for macOS so we can run unit tests on the Mac host. After adding onHingeChange behind if #available(iOS 27.1, *), the iOS build is fine but swift build on the Mac fails with "value of type 'FoldMeter.Content' has no member 'onHingeChange'". We're on Xcode 27.1. Why, and what's the minimal fix? Go ahead and fix it.
evals.expected_output: A fix that adds a compile-time platform gate around the hinge code, explaining that Xcode 27.1 ships the macOS 27.0 SDK, which does not declare the API, so #available cannot help.
expectations: Explains that Xcode 27.1 ships the macOS 27.0 SDK (xcrun --sdk macosx --show-sdk-version reports 27.0), which does not declare onHingeChange at all, so a runtime #available check cannot help — the declaration has to exist for the code to compile.

Adds a compile-time platform gate around the hinge code in FoldMeter.swift — #if os(iOS), or one that also keeps tvOS and visionOS — while keeping the runtime if #available(iOS 27.1, *) check for the iOS deployment target.
Frames it as a toolchain gap rather than a permanent rule: the API is annotated for macOS 27.1 as well, so the gate can be revisited when a macOS 27.1 SDK ships.
The compile-time gate is a platform condition (#if os(...)) rather than #if compiler(...) or #if canImport(...), and the hinge behaviour is kept on iOS.

evals.name: app-store-deadlines
evals.prompt: We'll submit LegacyNotes (evals/files/LegacyNotes) built with Xcode 27.1 next month. Leaving code aside, what App Store work does iPhone Duo add, and by when? Plan only.
evals.expected_output: The App Store items with dates and sources: iPhone Duo screenshot sizes for both displays, required from April 2027 (with the difference between the screenshot specifications' and the news post's wording), the iOS 27 SDK requirement from the same month, submissions open since October 5, and app previews as optional with an accepted-resolution row that does not match the displays.
expectations: Gives the iPhone Duo screenshot sizes for both displays in both orientations: 1398 × 2034 / 2034 × 1398 px (outer) and 2007 × 2853 / 2853 × 2007 px (inner), citing App Store Connect's screenshot specifications.

States that iPhone Duo screenshots become required in April 2027, and notes that the screenshot specifications limit this to apps using the iOS 27.1 SDK or later while Apple's October 5 news says any app submitted — so a build with Xcode 27.1 is covered under either wording.
Mentions that from April 2027 uploads must also be built with the iOS 27 SDK or later.

Treats app previews as optional and does not present 886 × 1920 / 1920 × 886 px as a fit for the iPhone Duo displays without flagging the aspect-ratio mismatch or the need to confirm in App Store Connect.
Does not invent requirements Apple has not stated (for example a mandatory app preview, or a deadline before April 2027).
No file in the project copy was modified.
